detail: LNWR formed (London & Birmingham + Grand Junction + Manchester & Birmingham). Paid-up on stock and shares GBP10.71m at 30 Jun 1846; consolidated stock GBP8.88m plus partly paid new shares; total nominal under the Consolidation Act GBP17.24m (+GBP4.69m Extension shares).
source: Tuck, The Railway Shareholder's Manual (8th ed., 1847), LNWR capital account (archive.org railwaysharehol00tuckgoog)

detail: Railways Act 1921 grouping: LNWR (which had absorbed the Lancashire & Yorkshire on 1 Jan 1922) and Midland become the London Midland & Scottish Railway (LMS). LMS ordinary stock traded 108 5/8-101 1/4 in 1923 and 106 1/8-94 3/4 in 1924 (close Dec 1924 102). LMS ordinary capital not read here.
source: IMM Dec 1925, 'Market prices in' table p.45

detail: North Eastern Railway into the London & North Eastern Railway (LNER).
GWR survives the grouping, absorbing the Welsh companies (Taff Vale, Barry, Cambrian, Rhymney...). Its consolidated ordinary stock rose from GBP37.08m (1920) to GBP42.86m (1925).
source: IMM Dec 1920 and Dec 1925 main tables

detail: Transport Act 1947: GWR, LMS, LNER and Southern vested in the British Transport Commission; shareholders received 3% British Transport Stock 1978-88 on the basis of Stock Exchange prices of 1945-46. Total BTS issued for the railway undertakings (excl. London Transport): GBP927,313,593 nominal. GWR's own compensation figure not found in this session.
source: HC Deb 27 Jan 1966 vol 723 cc136-7W; HC Deb 18 Nov 1946

detail: The big French railway companies' networks pass to the new SNCF (convention of 31 Aug 1937). The companies kept a minority stake in SNCF and survived as holding companies (Paris-Orleans later became the Rothschild holding Paris Orleans SA, today Rothschild & Co). Compensation terms and values not collected here.
source: standard histories (not verified in this session)

detail: Egypt (Law 285/1956) nationalises the Suez Canal Company's Egyptian assets. Heads of Agreement (29 Apr 1958, signed 13 Jul 1958): Egypt pays GBP(E)28.3m (incl. GBP(E)5.3m of tolls already held), 1959-64; the company keeps its assets outside Egypt and becomes the Compagnie Financiere de Suez (1958).
Compagnie de Suez absorbs Lyonnaise des Eaux and becomes Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux (renamed Suez 2001); suez id continues. End-1997 market value FRF 84bn (EUR 13bn), end-1998 FRF 170bn (EUR 26bn).
source: Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux, Document de reference 1998

detail: Gaz de France absorbs Suez (21 GdF shares for 22 Suez shares) to form GDF Suez (renamed Engie 2015). Combined value ~EUR90bn at the Sept 2007 agreement (French parliamentary record). Successor Engie (not on the worklist; companiesmarketcap slug 'engie').
source: Gaz de France/Suez joint release 3 Sep 2007; Assemblee nationale cr-cfiab 06-07/c0607016; OGJ 'Gaz de France, Suez merger finalized'

detail: New York Central merges into the Pennsylvania Railroad to form the Penn Central Transportation Co. (values at the merger not collected here).
Penn Central files for bankruptcy, then the largest in US history.
Great Northern, Northern Pacific (with the CB&Q and SP&S) merge into Burlington Northern Inc. (later BNSF, owned by Berkshire Hathaway since 2010).
Santa Fe Pacific Corp (the Atchison's parent since 1968/1983) merges with Burlington Northern to form Burlington Northern Santa Fe; ~$4.1bn deal value.
Union Pacific takes control of Southern Pacific Rail Corp: ~$4.0bn for the equity (cash and stock) plus ~$1.4bn debt = $5.4bn.
Canadian National takes control of Illinois Central Corp ($39/share, ~$2.4bn; agreed 10 Feb 1998).
Erie Railroad merges with the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western to form the Erie Lackawanna (into Conrail 1976). No values collected after 1882.
BP acquires Amoco (Standard Oil of Indiana): 3.97 BP shares per Amoco share; ~$48.2bn at announcement (11 Aug 1998), ~$56.9bn fair value at completion. BP Amoco plc.
source: FTC complaint Dec 1998; BP Amoco 20-F FY1998

detail: BP Amoco acquires Atlantic Richfield (ARCO): 9.84 BP shares per ARCO share, total consideration $27,506m (announced Apr 1999 at $26.8bn); ARCO Alaska sold to Phillips.
source: BP Amoco 20-F FY2000; Irish Times Apr 1999

detail: Canadian Pacific Ltd (the 1881 Canadian Pacific Railway Co., renamed 1971) splits into Canadian Pacific Railway Ltd, CP Ships, PanCanadian Energy, Fording and Fairmont Hotels. CP Ltd was worth ~$12.6bn (Aug 2001); the railway alone ~$2.7-3.1bn after the split (companiesmarketcap). The legal parent continued as Fairmont Hotels & Resorts; these files follow the railway.
Canadian Pacific takes control of Kansas City Southern; renamed Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC).

USX Corp (the 1901 U.S. Steel, renamed 1986) separates: the legal entity becomes Marathon Oil Corp ($9.28bn end-2001) and the steel business is spun off as a new United States Steel Corp ($1.62bn). These files follow the steel company from 2002. Marathon Oil was acquired by ConocoPhillips on 22 Nov 2024.
Nippon Steel completes the purchase of United States Steel at $55 per share (~$14bn equity; companiesmarketcap last value $12.4bn); delisted.
Guinness plc merges with Grand Metropolitan to form Diageo (agreement 11 May 1997; combined market value ~$36bn). Successor Diageo (companiesmarketcap slug 'diageo', $55.8bn in Nov 2026).
source: FTC complaint In re Guinness/Grand Met

detail: De Beers Consolidated Mines delisted: bought by DB Investments (Anglo American 45%, Oppenheimer family 40%, Botswana 15%); deal value not verified here. Aug 2012: Anglo American buys the Oppenheimers' 40% for $5.1bn (85% stake).

Imperial Group (Imperial Tobacco Co., renamed 1981) acquired by Hanson Trust (value not verified here). Oct 1996: Hanson demerges Imperial Tobacco Group plc (Imperial Brands since 2016), the company whose values from 2012 are in values.csv under the same id.

BAT Industries (British-American Tobacco Co., renamed 1976) splits: tobacco listed as British American Tobacco plc (values from 1998 under the same id); financial services merged with Zurich (Allied Zurich).
Rio Tinto Company merges with Consolidated Zinc to form the Rio Tinto-Zinc Corporation (RTZ); dual-listed with CRA from 1995, renamed Rio Tinto 1997.
Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp merges with Thyssen AG into ThyssenKrupp AG. Krupp was family/foundation-owned and never quoted on its own before the 1992 Hoesch takeover; no market values collected.
International Harvester (after selling its farm-equipment business to Tenneco, 1985) renamed Navistar International; values 2001-2020 from companiesmarketcap.
Navistar acquired by Traton (Volkswagen) at $44.50 per share (~$3.7bn equity, widely reported).
